## My report

The paper by Moreno-Medina, Ouss, Bayer and Ba measures obfuscatory language in US news reports on police killings and relates it to support for the police. In my report, I argue that their evidence shows a correlation between police and media language rather than police reports driving media coverage, and I suggest an analysis of evidential markers such as “police say” to test it. I also question the donation outcome used in their experiment, propose the CES panel to account for respondents’ media exposure, and point to other differences across media outlets worth examining.
